originalTitle: Australia news live: Acma takes Optus to court over triple-zero outage; bird flu reaches Victoria
content: The number of suspected deadly bird flu cases continues to grow in South Australia, with 13 more in greater crested terns, the state government said. Five of the new suspected H5N1 cases are at Seal Bay at Kangaroo Island, home to a population of endangered Australian sea lions. Victoria has also confirmed its first case of the disease in a greater crested tern – a common local seabird – found at Portland. Victoria’s chief veterinary officer, Graeme Cooke, said: We need Victorians to avoid contact with sick or dead wildlife, record what they see and report it. Early reporting gives us the best chance to reduce the impacts of the disease. The remaining eight South Australian birds were detected in Robe. The SA government said CSIRO had also confirmed another positive infection in a giant petrel. It follows Wednesday’s announcement of a suspected 11 cases in greater crested terns, including one at Seal Bay, where on-beach tours have temporarily been paused. An SA government spokesperson said they expected to have the CSIRO results for all 24 terns in coming days: South Australians are encouraged to continue being vigilant in reporting sick and dead birds and other wildlife. An 18-year-old woman has died in custody at the Dame Phyllis Frost Centre, with authorities saying the state coroner is investigating the circumstances of the teenager’s death. Corrections Victoria issued a statement on Tuesday in response to her death. We recognise that all deaths in custody have an impact on family members, friends and those working within the corrections system, as well as victims of crime. All deaths in custody are reported to the coroner’s court of Victoria, which formally determines the cause of death. The National Network of Incarcerated and Formerly Incarcerated Women and Girls’s Tabitha Lean said her death was a “tragedy” and urged greater support and trauma-informed care for vulnerable incarcerated individuals. An 18-year-old should be planning her future, not dying in prison. She was still a teenager. Her death should shock the conscience of every Australian. Every death in custody should propel this nation to act. Never has the call for decarceration been louder or more urgent. We cannot continue to accept prisons as the default response to the complex social and health issues faced by women and girls. This tragedy must be a turning point. The Australian Communications and Media Authority (Acma) has taken Optus to court over the September 2025 triple zero outage. A network firewall upgrade blocked emergency service calls for Optus customers in South Australia, Western Australia, the Northern Territory and parts of New South Wales, with more than 600 calls not able to connect in the 13 hours it was offline last year. Two deaths were linked to the outage, with people unable to connect to triple zero. The regulator announced on Thursday it had launched action in the federal court alleging Optus had breached two separate legal obligations on 1,005 occasions. Acma alleges that Optus failed to give end-users who made emergency calls access to the emergency call service, and to ensure emergency calls were carried to the relevant termination point. Acma chair, Nerida O’Loughlin said: Australians rightly expect that when they call triple zero, their call will connect. The circumstances of this outage meant that did not reliably occur, leaving people unable to connect to potentially life-saving services. Giving access to the emergency call service is not optional, it is a fundamental legal obligation and the most important public safety responsibility telecommunications providers have. Optus could face penalties of up to $250,000 per contravention. Optus has been approached for comment. Luke Gosling, the federal member for Solomon, has been arrested this morning over an alleged assault earlier this month, Northern Territory police said in a statement. “The Northern Territory Police Force has arrested the 54-year-old federal member for Solomon in relation to an alleged assault on the Administrator of the Northern Territory,” police said, adding: It is alleged the incident occurred at a public event on Saturday 18 July 2026 involving the 54-year-old and the Administrator of the Northern Territory. Investigations began last week and police arrested the 54-year-old earlier this morning and he remains in custody. A police spokesperson said Gosling had not yet been charged. Police said it related to an alleged incident regarding the NT’s administrator, David Connolly. Gosling has previously denied having any altercation with Connolly, and NT media reported Gosling as previously calling the claims “ridiculous allegations that I categorically deny”. The Guardian has reached out to Gosling’s office for further comment. Taylor runs dead on Icac questions The opposition leader, Angus Taylor, has dodged questions about the NSW Liberal party and an inquiry under way by the state’s corruption watchdog. Taylor, who is not accused of wrongdoing, was on Tuesday mentioned in Icac proceedings when Dylan Whitelaw, a former NSW Liberal parliamentary staffer and associate of the internal party group calling themselves the Reformers, gave evidence. During the hearing, Whitelaw was shown a screenshot of a message from the Catholic Schools NSW chief executive, Dallas McInerney. It suggested he was going to “shake down Angus for 10k”. The group wanted more conservative policies on same-sex marriage, abortion and euthanasia. Asked this morning in Queensland if he had ever given money to Catholic Schools NSW, Taylor avoided answering, repeating his same lines from Wednesday. “I’ve answered these questions yesterday. I’m not going to give a running commentary on it,” Taylor said. Taylor told media on Wednesday that no payments were made but did not answer further questions. chineseTitle: 澳大利亚新闻直播：Acma 将 Optus 因三零停电问题告上法庭；禽流感抵达维多利亚州
chineseContent: 州政府表示，南澳大利亚疑似致命禽流感病例数量持续增加，其中大凤头燕鸥病例新增 13 例。其中 5 例疑似 H5N1 病例发生在袋鼠岛海豹湾，那里是濒临灭绝的澳大利亚海狮的栖息地。维多利亚州还确认了首例这种疾病，患者是在波特兰发现的一种当地常见的海鸟——大凤头燕鸥。维多利亚州首席兽医官格雷姆·库克（Graeme Cooke）表示：我们需要维多利亚人避免接触生病或死亡的野生动物，记录他们所看到的情况并报告。早期报告为我们提供了减少疾病影响的最佳机会。其余八只南澳大利亚鸟类是在罗布发现的。南澳政府表示，澳大利亚联邦科学与工业研究组织（CSIRO）还确认了一只巨型海燕的另一例阳性感染病例。此前周三宣布疑似有 11 例大凤头燕鸥感染病例，其中一例发生在海豹湾，那里的海滩游览已暂时暂停。南澳政府发言人表示，他们预计将在未来几天内获得所有 24 只燕鸥的 CSIRO 结果：鼓励南澳人继续保持警惕，报告生病和死亡的鸟类和其他野生动物。一名 18 岁女子在菲利斯·弗罗斯特女爵士中心 (Dame Phyllis Frost Centre) 羁押期间死亡，当局称州验尸官正在调查这名少女的死亡情况。维多利亚惩教所周二就她的死亡发表声明。我们认识到，所有在押期间的死亡都会对家人、朋友、惩教系统内的工作人员以及犯罪受害者产生影响。所有在押期间的死亡都会报告给维多利亚验尸法庭，由该法庭正式确定死因。全国被监禁和曾经被监禁的妇女和女童网络
